abstract: Advances in generative AI have made it possible to produce music that is nearly indistinguishable from human compositions, raising the question of whether such works can be reliably distinguished from human compositions. We present MUSEBENCH, a large-scale benchmark for AI-generated music detection and artifact analysis, comprising over 361K tracks. The dataset includes human compositions, stylistically matched music generated by ten state-of-the-art open-source and commercial models, such as Suno and Udio, as well as human-AI co-creations and variants processed with adversarial perturbations, compression, and acoustic post-processing. Using MUSEBENCH, we benchmark 11 automated detectors and evaluate their accuracy, generalization, and robustness, under default, out-of-domain, and transformed-variant experiment settings. We further conduct a comprehensive artifact analysis through acoustic feature inspection, identifying recurring signatures such as non-idiomatic harmonic progressions, upsampling induced spectral periodicities, and violations of physical performance constraints. Our findings reveal key strengths and vulnerabilities of existing detectors and provide practical insights for building more reliable AI music detection systems.
oneSentenceThesis: MuseBench 用 361166 首曲目对照人类作曲与 10 种生成器输出，测出频谱图模型在干净条件下接近满分但在跨模型、压缩与变速下分化，并归纳出频谱、和声与演奏层面的可复现伪影线索与代价。
originalTitle: MUSEBENCH: A Benchmark for AI-Generated Music Detection and Artifact Analysis
readerTitle: MuseBench：大规模 AI 生成音乐检测与伪影分析基准
